sections.h2: Where do Henry County, KY owners go about property tax?
sections.html:
Owners deal with three separate counters in New Castle, and the one you need depends on whether the question is value, payment or a past-due bill.

  • Henry County PVA: 23 South Property Road, New Castle, KY 40050, mailing address P.O. Box 11, office phone (502) 845-5740. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The PVA handles assessments, ownership records and homestead applications.
  • Henry County Sheriff: (502) 845-2909. This office mails and collects the current tax bill, and the PVA's website links to the sheriff's bill search.
  • Henry County Clerk: 27 South Property Road, New Castle, mailing address P.O. Box 615, phone (502) 845-5705. The clerk is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and closes for lunch from noon to 1:00 p.m. Delinquent bills and deed recordings both go through this office, and it accepts eRecording.

The PVA's own site points out that a bill is issued to whoever held title on January 1. If you bought the house later in the year, the bill still comes in the former owner's name until the next calendar year, although the office tries to mail a copy to the new owner using recorded deeds. A buyer who has not seen a bill can call the sheriff and ask for the details.

sections.h2: What is Henry County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Henry County is a farm and commuter county in north central Kentucky, formed in 1798 from part of Shelby County and named for a Revolutionary War era statesman and governor of Virginia. New Castle is the seat, but Eminence is the largest city. The other cities are Campbellsburg, Pleasureville (partly in Shelby County) and Smithfield.

The county covers 291 square miles, and every resident was counted as living in a rural area at the 2020 census. The Kentucky River forms part of its border, and Carroll, Owen, Franklin, Shelby, Oldham and Trimble counties surround it. It belongs to the Louisville metropolitan area, and Wikipedia describes it as an increasingly important exurb since the 1990s, partly because land in neighboring Oldham County became more expensive.

The population grew from 15,678 in the 2020 census to an estimated 16,447 in 2025, a gain of 4.9 percent. Two public school systems operate here, Henry County Schools and the Eminence Independent district, so confirm which district covers your address when you write the listing.

The county runs on Eastern time, and the mean trip to work takes 30.5 minutes, longer than in Henderson or Hart County, which fits a commuter profile.

sections.h2: How is a Henry County property tax bill scheduled?
sections.html:
Kentucky's standard calendar applies: the bill is due by December 31 of the assessment year, with a discount early and penalties late. KRS 134.015 sets a 2 percent reduction for full payment by November 1, no adjustment between November 2 and December 31, a 5 percent penalty for January, and a 10 percent penalty after that.

The sheriff is the collector under KRS 134.119 and may accept full or partial payment until the unpaid claims are filed with the county clerk. Mail that was postmarked by the filing date is still processed at the earlier amount. Partial payments are divided among the taxing bodies on the bill in proportion to what each is owed.

When the state is late producing bills, it can switch to an alternative schedule with a discount for one month after mailing, face value for the second month and penalties after that.

sections.h2: Who can ask for a Henry County assessment to be reviewed?
sections.html:
The property owner can, and so can local officials. Under KRS 133.120, the board of assessment appeals may revise a value on the written recommendation of the county judge/executive, the mayor of a city that uses the county assessment, or the superintendent of the school district where the parcel lies. The Department of Revenue can also recommend a review.

For an owner, the path is a conference with the PVA first, then a written petition to the county clerk by one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals convenes between 25 and 35 days after the inspection period under KRS 133.030, sits as long as it needs to hear appeals, and normally stops after five days unless the state allows more time.

  • Prepare facts: land and building details, insurance policies, construction cost, listings, sale contracts and mortgages.
  • Expect the board to increase a value when evidence points that way. In that case the owner receives notice and a date to protest.
  • A taxpayer who thinks a neighbor's property is under-assessed may ask the board to review it, if that taxpayer listed their own parcel at fair cash value and supplies comparable sales or cost data in writing.
  • Blanket reviews of many properties are not allowed.

Filing an appeal never suspends payment. You owe tax on the value you claim, and any balance is billed afterward with interest.

sections.h2: How does the Henry County homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
It removes a fixed amount from the assessed value of the primary residence of an owner who is 65 or older, or who is classified as totally disabled. The PVA's site says to contact the office to see whether you qualify, and the state sets the 2025 and 2026 amount at $49,100.

On a house valued at the county's Census median of $197,900, the taxable assessment would drop to $148,800. Age can be proven with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. A disability claim rests on a federal or retirement-system classification and is renewed each year, with exceptions for service-connected veterans and for permanent Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rulings.

sections.h2: What happens to a Henry County tax debt if I sell?
sections.html:
The debt does not leave with you. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and the lien for delinquent taxes under KRS 134.420 continues for eleven years no matter who holds title afterward.

Ask the sheriff for a payoff on a current bill and the Henry County Clerk for any delinquent one, which the clerk's website lists under its delinquent taxes link. If the sheriff has filed unpaid claims with the clerk, KRS 134.119 adds the sheriff's collection fee, set at ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty, to what must be paid.

Deed recording runs through the clerk as well. The grantor owes Kentucky's real estate transfer tax of fifty cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050, or $198 on a $197,900 sale. The clerk collects it before accepting the deed, and keeps five percent as a collection fee before sending the rest to the county treasurer every three months.

faqs.q: Who is the tax collector in Henry County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Henry County Sheriff. Call (502) 845-2909 for bill questions. Delinquent bills sit with the Henry County Clerk at (502) 845-5705.

faqs.q: Why did my Henry County tax bill come in the previous owner's name?
faqs.a: Because Kentucky assesses and assigns ownership as of January 1. If you bought after that date, the bill stays in the former owner's name until the next calendar year.

faqs.q: How big is the Henry County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled. Apply through the Henry County PVA.

faqs.q: Can Henry County officials challenge my assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. The county judge/executive, a city mayor or a school superintendent can recommend in writing that the appeals board review a specific parcel, and so can the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What does the Henry County Clerk charge for transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state rate of $0.50 per $500 of value, paid by the seller when the deed is recorded. The clerk's recording fees are separate, so ask the office for the current amount.
